questions.prompt: When an int variable is passed to a normal C function parameter of type int, what is passed?
options: A reference to the original variable
questions.explanation: C uses pass-by-value for ordinary function arguments.

questions.prompt: After int x = 3; int y = x++; what are x and y?
questions.explanation: Post-increment yields the old value, then increments x.

questions.prompt: What does enum primarily define in C?
options: A set of named integer constants
questions.explanation: An enum introduces named integer constants.

questions.prompt: What is the type returned by the sizeof operator?
questions.explanation: sizeof returns a value of type size_t.

questions.prompt: A variable declared inside a block surrounded by braces generally has what scope?
questions.explanation: Variables declared inside a block generally have block scope.

questions.prompt: What does int marks[3] = {10, 20, 30}; initialize marks[1] to?
questions.explanation: Array indexing begins at 0, so marks[1] is the second element.

questions.prompt: Which format specifier is commonly used with printf to print a char as a character?
questions.explanation: %c prints a character value.

questions.prompt: What does a pointer variable store?
questions.explanation: A pointer stores the address of an object or function of a compatible type.

questions.prompt: If int x = 10; int *p = &x; what does *p evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Dereferencing p accesses the int object to which it points.

questions.prompt: Which statement about malloc is correct?
options: It returns a pointer to dynamically allocated memory or NULL
It allocates memory on the call stack
It can only allocate arrays of int
questions.explanation: malloc allocates uninitialized heap memory and may return NULL on failure.

questions.prompt: Which allocation function initializes the allocated bytes to zero?
questions.explanation: calloc allocates memory and initializes all bits to zero.

questions.prompt: What does strlen("hello") return?
questions.explanation: strlen counts characters before the terminating null byte.

questions.prompt: Inside the same scope as int a[10]; what does sizeof(a) usually represent?
options: The size of one element only
The total size of the entire array in bytes
The number of initialized elements only
questions.explanation: For an actual array object, sizeof gives the total number of bytes occupied by the array.

questions.prompt: When an array expression is passed to a function parameter declared as int arr[], what does the parameter actually receive?
options: A copy of the whole array
A pointer to the first element
A pointer to the last element
questions.explanation: Array parameters are adjusted to pointer parameters in function declarations.

questions.prompt: Which operator accesses a member through a pointer to a structure?
questions.explanation: p->member is equivalent to (*p).member for a structure pointer p.

questions.prompt: Which function is generally safer than gets for reading a bounded line into a buffer?
questions.explanation: fgets accepts a maximum buffer size and avoids the unbounded behavior of gets.

questions.prompt: A local variable declared static inside a function has what property?
options: It is re-created on every recursive call
It retains its value between function calls
questions.explanation: A static local has block scope but static storage duration.

questions.prompt: What does extern int count; usually indicate at file scope?
options: count is defined and initialized here
count is declared here and defined elsewhere
count is allocated on the stack
questions.explanation: extern can declare an object with external linkage without defining storage in that declaration.

questions.prompt: In const char *p, what is const?
options: The char object pointed to through p
questions.explanation: const char *p means p points to a char that should not be modified through p.

questions.prompt: If p is an int* pointing to a valid array element, what does p + 1 point to?
options: An unrelated address chosen by the compiler
questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic is scaled by the size of the pointed-to type.

questions.prompt: Which statement about void* in C is correct?
options: It can point to objects of different object types
It can be dereferenced directly to obtain a value
It always points to a function
questions.explanation: void* is a generic object pointer, but it must be converted to an appropriate pointer type before dereferencing.

questions.prompt: What does typedef do in C?
options: Creates an alias for a type
questions.explanation: typedef introduces an alternative name for an existing type.

questions.prompt: A union object provides storage that is generally shared by its members. What is its size at least large enough to hold?
options: Its largest member, plus any required padding
The sum of all members exactly
questions.explanation: A union must be able to store any one of its members.

questions.prompt: The controlling expression of a switch statement in C must be of which kind?
options: Integer type or compatible promoted type
questions.explanation: C switch statements operate on integer expressions after promotions.

questions.prompt: Which declaration declares fp as a pointer to a function taking an int and returning int?
questions.explanation: Parentheses around *fp make fp a pointer to a function.

questions.prompt: Why is a base case important in recursive C functions?
options: It prevents infinite recursion under normal conditions
questions.explanation: A base case provides a condition under which recursion stops.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between ++i and i++ when used as standalone statements?
options: No difference in final value of i
questions.explanation: As standalone statements, both increment i once; their yielded values differ only in larger expressions.

questions.prompt: What typically happens to char and short operands in many arithmetic expressions in C?
options: They are promoted to int or unsigned int
They are always converted to double
questions.explanation: Integer promotions convert smaller integer types to int or unsigned int where applicable.

questions.prompt: Why do C functions that accept arrays often also accept a length parameter?
options: Array length is always stored in the first element
The function usually receives only a pointer, not the array size
The compiler refuses arrays without length
The length is needed only for floating-point arrays
questions.explanation: Array-to-pointer adjustment loses the array bound information.

questions.prompt: What does fopen commonly return on failure?
questions.explanation: fopen returns a FILE* on success and NULL on failure.

questions.prompt: What happens when free(NULL) is called in C?
options: It is guaranteed to do nothing
questions.explanation: The C standard specifies that passing NULL to free has no effect.

questions.prompt: Which statement about realloc is correct?
options: It may return a different pointer and invalidate the old one on success
questions.explanation: realloc may move the allocation; if successful, the old pointer should no longer be used.

questions.prompt: Which function should be preferred over memcpy when source and destination ranges may overlap?
questions.explanation: memmove is designed to handle overlapping memory ranges.

questions.prompt: Why should macro parameters often be parenthesized in macro definitions?
options: To allocate them on the heap
To avoid precedence surprises in expanded expressions
questions.explanation: Parenthesizing macro parameters reduces incorrect grouping after expansion.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of an include guard in a header file?
questions.explanation: Include guards avoid repeated declarations or definitions from multiple includes.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes volatile in C?
options: It tells the compiler an object may change in ways not visible in ordinary code flow
It stores the object in ROM
questions.explanation: volatile affects optimization assumptions, but does not by itself provide atomicity or synchronization.

questions.prompt: In int main(int argc, char *argv[]), what does argc represent?
options: The number of command-line arguments including the program name
The size of argv in bytes
questions.explanation: argc is the count of command-line argument strings passed to the program.

questions.prompt: At file scope, what does static int helper; do to the name helper?
options: Exports it from every translation unit
questions.explanation: static at file scope gives the identifier internal linkage.

questions.prompt: What is the output-relevant issue with #define SQUARE(x) x * x when used as SQUARE(1 + 2)?
options: It expands to 1 + 2 * 1 + 2, causing precedence problems
It cannot compile because macros cannot use *
It converts the expression to double
questions.explanation: Without parentheses, macro expansion can change the intended grouping.

questions.prompt: What is the behavior of int i = 1; i = i++ + 1; in standard C?
questions.explanation: The expression modifies i and also reads it for another purpose without required sequencing.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with returning the address of a non-static local variable from a C function?
options: The pointer becomes invalid after the function returns
The variable is copied to the heap automatically
It is safe if the variable is int
questions.explanation: An automatic local object ceases to exist when its block/function lifetime ends.

questions.prompt: Which rule is most directly involved when an object is accessed through an incompatible pointer type?
options: The effective type / strict aliasing rule
questions.explanation: C restricts accessing stored values through incompatible lvalue types.

questions.prompt: What is the behavior of overflowing a signed int in standard C?
questions.explanation: Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in standard C.

questions.prompt: What is the issue with reading an uninitialized automatic int object?
options: It has an indeterminate value and reading it can cause undefined behavior
It reads the previous global variable
questions.explanation: Automatic objects without initialization have indeterminate values.

questions.prompt: What is sizeof("abc") in C?
questions.explanation: A string literal includes the terminating null character, so the array has four chars.

questions.prompt: What is the behavior of attempting to modify a string literal through char *s = "hi"; s[0] = 'H';?
options: A guaranteed compile-time error in all C modes
questions.explanation: String literals are not modifiable objects; attempting to modify one is undefined behavior.

questions.explanation: Containers such as vector can use noexcept moves instead of copies during growth.

questions.prompt: What does SFINAE stand for?
options: Substitution Failure Is Not An Error
Static Functions Initialize No Automatic Entities
Safe Function Inlining Needs Accurate Exceptions
questions.explanation: SFINAE allows invalid template substitutions to remove candidates instead of causing hard errors.

questions.prompt: What is template specialization?
options: Providing a custom implementation for particular template arguments
Turning a template into a macro
questions.explanation: Specialization customizes a template for specific arguments.

questions.prompt: Which utility is used to preserve the value category of a forwarding reference?
questions.explanation: std::forward<T>(x) conditionally casts based on T to preserve lvalue/rvalue-ness.

questions.prompt: Which binding can extend the lifetime of a temporary in a local declaration?
questions.explanation: Binding a temporary to a const lvalue reference in a local declaration extends its lifetime to the reference lifetime.

questions.prompt: What does the Rule of Zero encourage?
options: Design classes so they do not need custom destructors/copy/move operations
Always define five special member functions
Use only raw new and delete
Initialize all integers to zero manually
questions.explanation: Resource-owning behavior should be delegated to RAII members when possible.

questions.prompt: What is argument-dependent lookup (ADL)?
options: Name lookup that also considers namespaces associated with function argument types
A rule for integer promotions only
questions.explanation: ADL finds functions in namespaces associated with argument types.
